summary: Dedicated customer request: scheduled/automated weekly Usage Insights exports (CSV/JSON) for FinOps chargeback
description:
Issue summary
- Customer (Northwind Metrics, Dedicated) wants scheduled/automated exports for the new Usage Insights (cost drivers by route/model) to support weekly FinOps chargeback and internal reporting.

Customer request
- “Can Redwood email us a weekly CSV, or push exports to an S3 bucket? We want this per project + environment and need it to be repeatable.”
- Preferred cadence: weekly (Mon 09:00 local), with an option to backfill the prior week.
- Format: CSV primary, JSON acceptable.
- Filters: time range, project, environment, region, route, model.
- Access controls: must be auditable and respect RBAC (they have separate teams per project).

Impact
- Operational pain: today they are manually exporting from Console and pasting into internal sheets.
- They are trying to roll out chargeback policies and need consistent weekly reporting.
- Not a service outage; request is for automation.

Current product behavior / limitation
- Usage Insights supports on-demand exports (bounded by max time range/row limits) via Console export action; export/download is audit-logged.
- There is no built-in scheduled export / delivery (email/S3/webhook) in GA scope.

Ask from Support
- Confirm whether scheduled exports are on roadmap.
- Provide an interim workflow that is supportable for Dedicated customers.

Notes
- Customer explicitly asked whether automated exports would also generate audit events and whether service accounts are supported for automation.

Proposed next steps
- Triage as feature request (Product) and provide interim automation guidance using the export job API + customer-owned scheduler.
- Confirm guardrails (time range limits, file size, rate limits) and recommended batching/pagination approach.
- Offer Solutions Engineering office hours if they want to stand up a small weekly job quickly.

resolution: Scheduled exports (delivery/email/S3/webhook) are not available in the current Usage Insights export feature set. Provided an interim supported workflow: customer-run scheduler (cron) calling the export job API with stable filters, then downloading CSV/JSON and delivering to their own storage/reporting system. Confirmed audit logging + RBAC expectations and documented relevant limits. Feature request captured for Product to revisit post-GA stabilization.
customer_facing_response:
Thanks for reaching out — today Usage Insights supports on-demand exports (CSV/JSON) from the Console (and via the export job API), but we don’t yet offer a built-in “scheduled export” delivery feature (email/S3/webhook).

Interim workflow (supported)
- Run a weekly job in your environment (cron/GitHub Actions/etc.) that:
  1) calls the export job creation endpoint with your desired filters (project/environment/region/time range)
  2) polls job status until complete
  3) downloads the CSV/JSON
  4) uploads it to your internal destination (e.g., S3) and/or forwards internally

Security/audit/RBAC
- Export creation + download are audit-logged (who/when/filters), and access respects org/project RBAC. We recommend using a dedicated service account/token scoped to the relevant project(s).

Operational notes
- Keep exports to a bounded time range and split by project/environment if needed to stay within file size/row limits.

If helpful, we can set up a short session to walk through the recommended API usage pattern for a weekly job.
internal_notes: Feature request only (not a bug). If this becomes common, consider a standardized one-pager for enterprise security reviews: scheduled exports not supported; automation via API is supported; audit logging applies to export actions. Customer likely to ask next about: (1) long-range exports, (2) invoice reconciliation, (3) pushing exports to customer bucket. Point them to export limits + known invoice mismatch explanations if needed.
